featured_reviews.name: Harsh Gajera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a great experience at Take and Treat! The ambience is peaceful and well-maintained, ideal for family dinners or casual meals.🍾🤤

Their soya chaap is hands down the best item — delicious, tender, and seasoned with authentic masala. The option to order half or full is perfect for managing portions. 🍕🍻

The quantity is generous, and you definitely get your money’s worth. Every dish tastes fresh and rich in flavour without being overly spicy. The staff is polite, and the service is quick. Prices are super affordable, which makes it a go-to spot for everyday dining. Coffee is smooth and aromatic, and the lemon tea is soothing after a spicy meal. 🫶🏻

The overall vibe is homely and comfortable.
If you love authentic North Indian-style flavours and want something light on the pocket, this place won’t disappoint. Definitely recommending it to friends!🤟🤟

featured_reviews.name: Vinit Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Take and Treat is a hidden gem for food lovers looking for great taste at affordable rates.
The ambience is simple yet clean, giving a cozy local restaurant vibe. The staff is attentive and ensures your food is served hot and fresh.
Their soya chaap is the star — soft, flavorful, and perfectly cooked, with both half and full portions available.
You can really taste the authenticity in their spices and preparation. The rest of the menu is also impressive, with decent variety and generous portions.
Every dish feels like it’s made with care, not rushed. The rates are pocket-friendly, making it perfect for students and working people. The coffee is creamy and comforting, while the lemon tea is refreshing after a heavy meal.
It’s rare to find such quality food at this price. Great for both dine-in and takeaway — Take and Treat truly lives up to its name!

featured_reviews.name: Hasmukh Mali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Premji’s Fast Food & Soda Center is a well-known local favorite, especially if you’re craving a flavorful plate of pav bhaji or a refreshing glass of soda. The taste truly stands out – the pav bhaji is rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced, and the variety of soda options makes it a great stop for a quick refreshment.

The place has a lively street-food vibe, and it’s clear that they’ve built a solid reputation over time. The pricing is reasonable, and the quality is consistent, which explains the heavy footfall every evening.

That said, be prepared for a long wait during peak hours, especially at night. The queue can get quite long, and the waiting period may test your patience. Seating is limited, and it’s more of a stand-and-eat or take-away kind of place.

If you’re not in a rush and want to enjoy tasty street food at a reasonable price, this spot is definitely worth a visit. Just try to go during off-peak hours if you want to avoid the crowd!

featured_reviews.name: Umair Lucky
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you live in Mira Road, Nihal Corner isn’t just a restaurant; it’s a milestone. While most places are winding down, this corner of Naya Nagar is just waking up. Here is the "insider" take on how to do it right.
1. The "Off-Menu" Energy
While everyone talks about the Seekh Paratha, the real pro-move is the Keema Ghotala for a late-night protein hit. It’s oily, spicy, and perfectly messy. If you're there for breakfast (they open early!), pair their Maska Pav with a strong tea—it’s the most underrated "chill" vibe in the area.
2. The Seating Strategy
The Outdoor Hustle: Best if you want to soak in the Naya Nagar street life. You’ll hear the sizzle of the tandoor and the roar of bikes. It’s authentic, but expect a bit of smoke.
The AC Sanctuary: If you’re with family or want to actually hear your friends speak, pay the small premium for the AC section. It’s much more "cozy" and reliable for a relaxed meal.
3. The "Sweet" Finish
Don't just leave after the spice. Their Arabic Pudding and Caramel Custard are kept chilled and act as the perfect fire extinguisher for your palate.
The Reality Check:
Hygiene: It’s a busy, high-turnover joint. If you’re looking for white-tablecloth fine dining, this isn't it. It’s "street-chic"—rugged and focused entirely on the taste.
Service: The waiters move like lightning because the crowd is relentless. Be firm with your order and don't expect a long chat.
Portions: Unlike many places that are shrinking sizes, Nihal still gives you a "family-sized" feel for a "bachelor’s budget."
Quick Specs:
Must Try: Seekh Paratha, Keema Ghotala, Mutton Samosa.
Price for two: ₹400–₹500 (You'll leave stuffed).
Parking: Almost non-existent for cars; bring a bike or take a rickshaw.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered from these guys after a long time through Zomato. I used to order regularly during the lockdown until i found some quality issues with their regular chicken shawarma and stopped ordering.

Last Saturday, I ordered a Chipotle shawarma as an evening snack. The order arrived before time. The Shawarma was delicious. I liked how the Chipotle sauce blended nicely with the garlic sauce and the chicken which was juicy and mildly smokey. I also loved the addition of what i think was lettuce and red (purple) cabbage. I totally enjoyed it and couldn't stop raving about it to my family.

Today, (Monday) my wife and i were craving for a Shawarma. I suggested getting the shawarmas from National Shawarma. Basis my last experience with how they prepared the Chipotle shawarma, I wanted to reorder from them. My wife prefers the shawarmas from Shawarma cafe. Lately, we had a few not so good experiences with the food we ordered from them, so we decided to take a break.

I went to the National Shawarma outlet near the station. Since it was past 8.30 PM, it was quite crowded. I ordered the Chipotle and Tandoori shawarma. My wife asked for the Tandoori shawarma as I had given her very good feedback about the Shawarma i ordered via Zomato.

While the shawarmas were being prepared (Their preparation time is really fast) i noticed that the person making the shawarmas was adding green cabbage to the Chipotle shawarma. I didn't see any lettuce or the red cabbage being added like it was when i ordered from Zomato. I didn't get a chance to see how the tandoori shawarma was prepared as I got distracted for a bit. Anyway, i did not ask the guy who took my order (I guess he was the owner) why it was being prepared differently as he was handling multiple customers/orders at the same time. I paid 200 in total. (100 for each shawarma)

Got the shawarmas home and to our dismay, the shawarmas were a big letdown  . The Chipotle shawarma was the real disappointment as it was nowhere close to the one I ordered off Zomato. I know there was not lettuce, red cabbage, but the chicken was quite chewy and that charred/smoked taste which i loved last time was missing for most part of the Shawarma. The Shawarma was heavily saucy which wasn't the case last time.

The tandoori chicken disappointed too. Pretty much the same experience with taste. To make matters worse, my partner found a few fragments of bone in her shawarma which put her off and she didn't finish the Shawarma.

To sum it all up, there was a stark difference in the Shawarma i ordered from Zomato vs. what we ate when we ordered from them directly. Frankly, the "Premium-ness" of their fusion shawarmas was missing by a mile.

I didn't expect this from National Shawarma specially when i decided to give them a second chance.

I will never order again.

P.S. I didn't click pictures as i didn't want to post them publically. Maybe i should have.

I would definitely not recommend having shawarma here.

Thank you for your response.
My concern is not about the MRP of Thums Up, which is clearly ₹20 (tax included).
The issue is that GST has again been applied on the total bill amount, including the cold drink, which already has GST included in its MRP.
As per GST rules, packaged beverages sold at MRP should not be taxed again.
I hope you will look into this billing practice to avoid confusion for customers in the future.

As per GST Act Section 15 and Notification 11/2017, packaged beverages sold at MRP already include GST and should not be subjected to restaurant service GST again.
